outgoing.explanation: The sole-personal-record analysis rests on the 1653 deposition being the one record to state John's own attribute (his age).
The broad footprint is property/office-heavy; the man himself is attested by a single line, qualifying how personal the coverage is.

finding.shortLabel: Analysis: the 1653 deposition is the only record of John's own person
finding.statement: The 1653 Wilson v. Faxon deposition ('John Gurney of Brayntree aged 50 Yeares or thereabouts') is the only surviving record that attests a personal attribute of John Gurney himself; every other record fixes his property, credit, or a civic/probate office rather than his person. A man documented across four record classes over two decades is thus attested as a person, as opposed to as a landholder, creditor, or estate, by a single line in one court file. (The weight of the stated age and its birth inference are worked in the origin/age analysis, not here.)
